cards.name: Constant gravity on vertical speed
cards.summary: A single gravity constant is subtracted from vertical speed every update, scaled by the frame step.
cards.behavior: Every object on the physical base carries a vertical speed in world units per frame. Before integration, the update subtracts the gravity constant multiplied by the current frame time from that vertical speed, so a fall accelerates at a fixed rate independent of mass. Horizontal speed is untouched by this step. The same path runs for vehicles, pedestrians and loose props, which keeps a dropped object and a falling car on identical acceleration.

constants.name: gravity
constants.unit: world units per frame per frame at the 30 Hz target update (frame-step scaled)

cards.name: Suspension spring and damping impulses
cards.summary: Compressed suspension emits a doubled spring impulse plus a damped impulse, with the frame step clamped.
cards.behavior: A compressed suspension point builds an upward impulse from gravity, body mass, the frame step, the spring constant, the compression ratio and a bias that is doubled inside the impulse. A second impulse removes a fraction of the average contact speed along the spring direction, again scaled by mass and the frame step. The frame step used by both impulses is clamped to three frames so a long hitch cannot inject unbounded energy. The damping factor 0.53 stops the spring from ringing under repeated contact.

constants.name: springBias
constants.unit: multiplier on the spring impulse, applied per frame at 30 Hz

constants.name: stepClamp
constants.unit: frames (maximum frame step used by the impulse) at 30 Hz

constants.name: dampingFactor
constants.unit: fraction of average contact speed removed per frame at 30 Hz

cards.name: Automatic gear shift thresholds
cards.summary: Gear bands are divided evenly; upshift at two thirds of a band, downshift at forty-two percent.
cards.behavior: Gear ratios are laid out as equally spaced speed bands between zero and the handling record top speed. The box requests an upshift once road speed passes 0.6667 of the current band above its lower edge, and a downshift once speed drops below 0.42 of the band. Reverse has its shift-up threshold set just below zero, so the transmission only leaves reverse when the car has essentially stopped or is already rolling forward.

constants.name: shiftUpFraction
constants.unit: fraction of a gear speed band, evaluated per update at 30 Hz

constants.name: shiftDownFraction
constants.unit: fraction of a gear speed band, evaluated per update at 30 Hz

constants.name: reverseShiftUpSpeed
constants.unit: world units per frame at 30 Hz

cards.name: Brake force and axle bias
cards.summary: Brake impulse scales with pedal, deceleration and frame step; normal cars double the handling bias.
cards.behavior: Each update turns the brake pedal position into an impulse by multiplying it by the handling record brake deceleration and the frame step. For player and remote-player cars the front bias is twice the handling bias, and the rear share is derived by subtracting that front value from two. When the same handling record is used by a non-player car flagged for neutral handling, both axles collapse to a bias of one and the car brakes evenly instead of nose-down.

constants.name: playerBrakeBiasScale
constants.unit: multiplier on the handling brake bias, applied per frame at 30 Hz

cards.name: Standing burnout trigger
cards.summary: Holding both pedals past 150 of 255 while nearly stopped arms a burnout and feeds both pedals.
cards.behavior: While absolute speed is below 0.01 the input stage checks whether accelerate and brake are both held above 150 on the 255-scale pad. If they are, the gas and brake pedals receive their normalized raw values and a burnout flag is raised; if not, the brake pedal is cleared. The flag later lets a rear-wheel-drive car cut rear brake and traction and apply a small yaw torque, which turns a stationary launch into wheelspin and rotation instead of a clean start.

constants.name: standstillSpeed
constants.unit: world units per frame at 30 Hz

constants.name: burnoutPedalThreshold
constants.unit: raw pad units on a 0-255 axis, sampled per frame at 30 Hz

constants.name: padFullScale
constants.unit: raw pad units at the top of the axis, sampled per frame at 30 Hz

cards.name: Steering input ramp and clamp
cards.summary: Steering chases the pad axis at twenty percent per frame step and clamps to a unit range.
cards.behavior: The left-right pad axis is divided by 128 to produce a signed target, and the carried steering input moves toward that target by 0.2 multiplied by the frame step. The result is clamped to plus or minus one, so held input cannot exceed full lock and a quick tap cannot jump straight to it. Mouse steering uses the same carried value with separate centering constants, keeping every input device on one normalized scale that the wheel model can consume.

constants.name: steerRampRate
constants.unit: fraction of the remaining error closed per frame at 30 Hz (frame-step scaled)

constants.name: padAxisScale
constants.unit: raw pad units per unit of steering input, sampled per frame at 30 Hz

constants.name: steerClamp
constants.unit: normalized steering input, applied per frame at 30 Hz

cards.name: Burnout yaw torque
cards.summary: A rear-drive burnout applies a small steer-scaled turn force at the rear-left contact.
cards.behavior: When a burnout is active and the handling record marks the car as rear-wheel drive, rear brake and rear traction are zeroed and a turn force is applied at the rear-left contact point. The force is minus 0.001 times the body turn mass times the current steer angle, directed along the car right vector. Because the coefficient is small, the result is a slow rotation into the steered direction rather than an instant spin, which lets a player hold a donut with steady input.

constants.name: burnoutYawCoefficient
constants.unit: negative turn force per unit turn mass and steer angle, applied per frame at 30 Hz

cards.name: Component damage thresholds
cards.summary: Hits are scaled per component group; 150 registers damage and 220 on front parts can reach the engine.
cards.behavior: Incoming impact damage is first multiplied by a per-group factor, and windscreen hits take an extra 0.6 scale. A hit only registers component damage above 150; below that the damage state is untouched, so light scrapes do not accumulate. Bonnet hits above 220, and front panel or windscreen hits above 220, also advance engine damage, which links bodywork placement to mechanical failure instead of treating every impact the same.

constants.name: componentDamageThreshold
constants.unit: damage units per impact, evaluated per collision event

constants.name: engineDamageThreshold
constants.unit: damage units per impact, evaluated per collision event

constants.name: windscreenDamageScale
constants.unit: multiplier on windscreen damage, applied per collision event

cards.name: Motorcycle lean and wheelie authority
cards.summary: Lean input ramps at twenty percent per step, clamps to one, and scales torque by min(speed, 0.1).
cards.behavior: Vertical pad input builds a lean value by closing twenty percent of the gap to the target each frame step, then clamps the result to plus or minus one. The lean torque uses the smaller of current speed magnitude and 0.1, so a wheelie or stoppie loses authority as soon as the bike is moving quickly and stays controllable at parking speeds. The gas pedal blends part of the force on the sport bike and an even split on other bikes, giving each model a different balance point.

constants.name: leanRampRate
constants.unit: fraction of the remaining error closed per frame at 30 Hz (frame-step scaled)

constants.name: leanSpeedCap
constants.unit: world units per frame at 30 Hz

constants.name: leanClamp
constants.unit: normalized lean input, applied per frame at 30 Hz

cards.name: Flying speed clamps and yaw damping
cards.summary: Flying bodies damp yaw by 0.9 per frame step and clamp linear speed to 1.5 and turn speed to 0.2.
cards.behavior: In the flying branch the yaw component of turn speed is multiplied by 0.9 raised to the frame step, which makes the damping independent of frame length. Linear speed magnitude is then clamped to 1.5 and turn speed magnitude to 0.2 by scaling the whole vector when it exceeds either limit. The two clamps keep aircraft and airborne cars inside the range where the shared solver stays stable, and they also cap how fast a player can cross the map in a helicopter or plane.

constants.name: yawDampingBase
constants.unit: ratio per frame at 30 Hz (raised to the frame step)

constants.name: maxLinearSpeed
constants.unit: world units per frame at 30 Hz

constants.name: maxTurnSpeed
constants.unit: radians per frame at 30 Hz

cards.name: Buoyancy decay while afloat
cards.summary: A floating boat loses one percent of its buoyancy accumulator every update.
cards.behavior: While a boat is in water its buoyancy value is multiplied by 0.99 on every update, pulling the hull toward its float equilibrium. Damage and ground contact feed the same accumulator through the damage impulse path, so a grounded or damaged boat recovers its float level over several seconds instead of snapping back. The decay runs before the boat control inputs, which means thrust and steering act on an already settling hull.

constants.name: buoyancyDecay
constants.unit: ratio per frame at 30 Hz

cards.name: Follow camera heights and interpolation
cards.summary: Third-person framing uses a 1.85 unit ground clearance, three zoom heights and 0.25/0.75 interpolation stops.
cards.behavior: The follow camera starts with a minimum ground distance of 1.85 units and three ground zoom heights of 0.25, 1.5 and 4.0 units. Height and zoom interpolation stop moving at a 0.25 fraction of the target and catch up at 0.75, while a 0.85 gait sway buffer smooths walking bob. A buffered height and height speed are kept on the camera so kerbs, stairs and suspension movement do not snap the view between frames.

constants.name: minGroundDistance
constants.unit: world units, static framing value sampled per frame at 30 Hz

constants.name: zoomHeightOne
constants.unit: world units above the target, static framing value sampled per frame at 30 Hz

constants.name: zoomHeightTwo
constants.unit: world units above the target, static framing value sampled per frame at 30 Hz

constants.name: zoomHeightThree
constants.unit: world units above the target, static framing value sampled per frame at 30 Hz

constants.name: stopMovingFraction
constants.unit: fraction of the interpolation target, evaluated per frame at 30 Hz

constants.name: catchUpFraction
constants.unit: fraction of the interpolation target, evaluated per frame at 30 Hz

cards.name: Sprint stamina drain and growth
cards.summary: Sprint drains one unit per frame to a -150 floor; every 500 progress units raise the 1000 cap by 10.
cards.behavior: Each sprinting update subtracts one stamina unit and adds one unit to a progress counter. Sprint becomes unavailable once stamina reaches -150, and every 500 units of progress reset the counter and raise maximum stamina by 10 up to a ceiling of 1000. Outside a sprint, recovery adds restore speed times the frame step times 0.5 until current stamina meets the maximum, so a long sprint is paid back over roughly twice the time it took to spend.

constants.name: staminaFloor
constants.unit: stamina units, static threshold checked per frame at 30 Hz

constants.name: refillProgress
constants.unit: stamina progress units per frame at 30 Hz

constants.name: maxStaminaCeiling
constants.unit: stamina units, static cap checked per frame at 30 Hz

constants.name: maxStaminaStep
constants.unit: stamina units granted per 500 progress units

constants.name: recoveryScale
constants.unit: multiplier on restore speed per frame at 30 Hz (frame-step scaled)

cards.name: Running landing and glide fade
cards.summary: A moving fall becomes a jump-land clip above 1.5 speed; glide clips fade with fixed blend deltas.
cards.behavior: A fall-land animation is replaced by the jump-land clip when the player is still moving faster than 1.5 units per frame and is pressing a movement axis. The old clip is faded out with a blend delta of -1000, making the switch immediate rather than a visible cross-fade. Releasing a glide or fall-glide clip uses a blend delta of -3.0, which fades it over several frames and keeps a short hop from popping.

constants.name: landingSpeedThreshold
constants.unit: world units per frame at 30 Hz

constants.name: landingBlendDelta
constants.unit: animation blend rate per frame at 30 Hz

constants.name: glideBlendDelta
constants.unit: animation blend rate per frame at 30 Hz

cards.name: Instant-hit torso damage
cards.summary: A pedestrian torso hit applies 3.5 times weapon damage and registers the shooter with flag 3.
cards.behavior: When an instant-hit trace crosses a pedestrian, the weapon applies damage to the torso; this path passes 3.5 times the weapon damage value. The shooter damage-entity pointer is registered on the victim the first time, and a local flag of 3 records that the hit has been registered. Occupants of vehicles take a separate branch, so a shot into a car routes damage to the vehicle instead of duplicating it on the driver.

constants.name: torsoDamageMultiplier
constants.unit: multiplier on weapon damage per hit

constants.name: damageRegistrationFlag
constants.unit: enum flag set once per hit

cards.name: Traffic cruise speed targets
cards.summary: Ambulance return cruises at 17, go-to-coordinate driving at 20 and parking at 10.
cards.behavior: An ambulance that has finished an accident response rejoins the road system with a cruise target of 17. A car sent to a coordinate receives 20, while a car asked to park receives 10. The autopilot consumes these targets as its speed setpoint for the current mission, so one driving loop covers emergency returns, ordinary destinations and parking maneuvers with only the target changing between them.

constants.name: ambulanceReturnCruise
constants.unit: cruise speed target units, applied per update, rate unverified

constants.name: goToCoordinateCruise
constants.unit: cruise speed target units, applied per update, rate unverified

constants.name: parkAtCoordinateCruise
constants.unit: cruise speed target units, applied per update, rate unverified
